_note: Search space of scripts/patient_cmaes_fit.py: the parametrisation of the CMA-ES fit of StuppFKPPSolver to one SAILOR patient (2026-09-25). It is read by that script's own reader, not by the atlas loader of scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py: keys starting with '_' are comments; an entry {"min", "max", "scale"} ("log": 10 ** (log10 min + u (log10 max - log10 min)), "linear": min + u (max - min), u the unit-cube coordinate) is a fitted factor; any other entry is a fixed value, written into every run config when it is a solver parameter (diffusivity_ratio, rt_alpha_beta_ratio, chemo_decay_rate, gaussian_seed_scale) or consumed by the script's derivations when it is not (seed_peak_density); "solver" is checked. The order of the factor entries is the coordinate order of the unit cube the optimizer works on. Six of the nine factors are script factors from which the script derives solver parameters per evaluation: front_speed_mm_per_day and front_width_mm give white_matter_diffusivity and rho (see _growth_band), seed_sigma_mm with the fixed seed_peak_density gives gaussian_seed_mass and gaussian_seed_diffusion_time (see _seed_band), growth_length_mm with the front speed gives the seed-to-pre-op interval preop_time and with it the whole clinical timeline (see _clock), and seed_bbox_x/y/z place the seed inside the bounding box of the pre-op tumour core (see _seed_position); rt_alpha and chemo_kill_rate are solver parameters written directly. The timeline entries (resection_time, time_after_resection, chemo_times, chemo_doses, rt_times, snapshot_times), the tissue maps, resection_cavity, rt_dose, the time step (n_steps, dt, steps_per_day), resolution_factor, the seed fractions and the derived parameters may not appear here: the script sets them per evaluation. Everything not listed comes from the base config given on the command line (fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json by default).
_revision: Derived on 2026-09-25 from sailor_patient_v2_search_space.json (2026-09-17, the search space of the sub-01 sensitivity sweeps sa_sub01_2026-09-16), with these changes. (1) The fitted set is reduced from twelve solver-relevant factors to nine: rt_alpha_beta_ratio (4-12 Gy), seed_peak_density (0.6-1.0) and diffusivity_ratio (1-100) are fixed, at 8 Gy, 0.6 and 10, because the sensitivity analysis found them inert on the agreement QoIs, so fitting them would spend evaluations on directions the objective does not see; the fixed values are the sweep space's midpoint (alpha/beta), its floor (the seed peak, a seed whose core just reaches the 0.6 enhancing threshold) and its geometric centre (the diffusivity ratio). (2) preop_time (30-200 days, uniform) is replaced by growth_length_mm = front_speed_mm_per_day x preop_time (0.21-50 mm, log-uniform), the distance the front travels before the pre-op scan, and preop_time = growth_length_mm / front_speed_mm_per_day is clamped by the script to [7, 200] days (see _clock); 0.21 = 0.03 x 7 and 50 = 0.25 x 200 are the hull of the corner products, so the clamp keeps every point admissible. (3) Three floors are widened toward the absence of an effect: the pre-op interval floor from 30 to 7 days (through growth_length_mm and the clamp; a tumour first imaged a week after the seed is the limit of a small, fast pre-op tumour), rt_alpha from 5e-4 to 1e-5 /Gy and chemo_kill_rate from 5e-5 to 1e-5 /day per mg/m^2, so that the optimizer can reach a radiotherapy or chemotherapy without a measurable effect on the model core instead of stopping at a floor. (4) The two threshold factors of the sweep space (core_threshold, edema_threshold_ratio) are gone: the fit profiles the thresholds on the sweep's grids per evaluation. Every other range and scale (front speed 0.03-0.25 mm/day, front width 1-8 mm, seed width 5-16 mm, rt_alpha and chemo_kill_rate caps, chemo_decay_rate 9.24, gaussian_seed_scale 1) is that of sailor_patient_v2_search_space.json.
_scales: Rate and scale parameters whose range spans a decade or more are sampled log-uniformly (front_speed_mm_per_day, chemo_kill_rate, rt_alpha, growth_length_mm: the response is expected to depend on their order of magnitude, and a uniform coordinate would spend most of the unit interval in the top decade); the front width front_width_mm is log-uniform as well over its 0.9 decades, and so is the seed width seed_sigma_mm over its 0.5 decades. The three seed position coordinates are linear on [0, 1] by construction (see _seed_position).
_growth_band: The growth dynamics are not fitted as a (white_matter_diffusivity, rho) rectangle but through the front: the Fisher-KPP front moves at v = 2 sqrt(D rho) and has the width lambda = sqrt(D / rho), and the script fits v = front_speed_mm_per_day (0.03-0.25 mm/day, log-uniform) and lambda = front_width_mm (1-8 mm, log-uniform) and derives D = v lambda / 2 and rho = v / (2 lambda). The velocity bound is the point: 0.25 mm/day is above the fastest radial expansion reported for glioblastoma (about 0.2 mm/day), so no run outgrows the brain within the horizon, whereas the corners of a (D, rho) rectangle covering the same cohort are not admissible tumors and dominated the variance of the 2026-09-08 atlas sweep. The front width is capped at 8 mm (2026-09-17) so that the model can produce the patient's whole-tumour to core volume ratio of about 5, which only 12 % of the rows of the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep reached with lambda <= 4 mm; the band still includes the GliODIL cohort's typical front of about 3.2 mm, and the 1 mm grid cannot resolve a front narrower than 1 mm. The implied ranges are D in [0.015, 1.0] mm^2/day and rho in [0.001875, 0.125] /day.
_clock: growth_length_mm (0.21-50 mm, log-uniform) is the distance the front has travelled when the patient is imaged before surgery: the script sets the seed-to-pre-op interval preop_time = growth_length_mm / front_speed_mm_per_day (days) and clamps it to the range given on the command line (--preop-time-range, default 7-200 days), recording whether the clamp was active. The pre-op scan is then at model day t_pre = preop_time (the seed is day 0) and every later event of the patient's calendar (resection three days before the post-op scan, the radiotherapy fractions, the temozolomide days, the adjuvant cycles and the scan of every session) is at t_pre + (calendar date - pre-op date) in days, so the whole treated stage shifts with it, exactly as in the sensitivity analysis. The length rather than the time is fitted because the pre-op tumour size is what the pre-op segmentation constrains: at a given size the speed and the interval are confounded, and a log-uniform length puts the optimizer's coordinate on the constrained quantity. The range is the hull of the corner products of the speed range and the interval range (0.03 x 7, 0.25 x 200), so every unit-cube point maps to an interval the clamp accepts, and the clamp binds only where the length and the speed together would leave the interval range.
_seed: The seed is a clipped Gaussian, c0(r) = m / (4 pi tau)^(3/2) exp(-r^2 / (4 tau)) with r the distance from the seed voxel in mm (gaussian_seed_scale = 1, fixed below; the solver multiplies voxel offsets by the grid spacing), values at or below gaussian_seed_floor zeroed and values above 1 clipped. Its shape and size follow from seed_peak_density (fixed) and seed_sigma_mm (fitted), see _seed_band; its position from seed_bbox_x/y/z, see _seed_position.
_seed_band: The seed's mass m (gaussian_seed_mass) and width tau (gaussian_seed_diffusion_time, mm^2 at gaussian_seed_scale = 1: the profile's standard deviation is sigma = sqrt(2 tau)) are not fitted independently: the floor and the clip act on the peak c_peak = m / (4 pi tau)^(3/2), so independent draws of m and tau over decades give seeds that are erased entirely or flattened to a clipped plateau. Instead the peak density seed_peak_density = c_peak is fixed at 0.6 (at the 0.6 enhancing threshold, so every seed has an enhancing core, and at the floor of the sweep space's 0.6-1.0 band, which the sensitivity analysis found inert) and the width sigma = seed_sigma_mm in mm is fitted directly (5-16 mm, log-uniform: the floor 5 mm includes GliODIL's default seed width, Dt = 15 mm^2 and M = 1500, i.e. sigma = 5.48 mm, and the cap 16 mm trims the tail of pre-operative sizes; the 2026-09-14 sweep had shown that 20 mm seeds grown for 30-200 days give brain-filling pre-op tumours), and the script derives gaussian_seed_diffusion_time = sigma^2 / 2 and gaussian_seed_mass = c_peak (4 pi tau)^(3/2), so every seed is a real Gaussian with that peak and width. The script checks the fixed peak against the base config's gaussian_seed_floor (0.1 in fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json) and the clip at 1 at start-up, and that gaussian_seed_scale is 1. With lambda in 1-8 mm and sigma in 5-16 mm the ratio s = sigma / lambda reaches down to 0.625: a seed narrower than about twice the front width is flattened by diffusion before the front forms; with the patient's mask cavity there is no seed-erosion failure mode, a flattened seed shows as an empty model core, a Dice of 0 against the pre-op reference. The 5-16 mm range is a design choice, not a literature value.
_seed_position: seed_bbox_x, seed_bbox_y and seed_bbox_z (linear on [0, 1]) place the seed inside the axis-aligned bounding box of the seedable voxels: the voxels of the pre-op tumour core (labels 1 necrotic and 3 enhancing of the pre-op segmentation, label 4 relabelled to 3 first) carrying tissue (wm + gm >= min_tissue_fraction, the solver's flux threshold as resolved from the base config), the same set the sensitivity analysis seeds in. With lo and hi the inclusive index bounds of the seedable voxels per axis, the point p = lo + u (hi - lo) in voxel coordinates is rounded to the nearest voxel; when that voxel is not seedable it is replaced by the nearest seedable voxel in Euclidean voxel distance (recorded as seed_snapped). The seed voxel's fractions (v + 0.5) / n go into the run config as gaussian_seed_{x,y,z}_fraction, as the sensitivity analysis writes them. Unlike the sweep's nested-range mapping, which is a measure-preserving map for a Sobol' design but not continuous, this map is continuous in u on the box, which is what a covariance-adapting optimizer needs; the two agree on the voxel they name, so a sweep row's seed voxel converts back into box coordinates exactly.
_chemo: The chemotherapy model's total log kill over the schedule is L = chemo_kill_rate * D_tot / chemo_decay_rate with D_tot the sum of the chemo_doses within the horizon, which here is the patient's schedule up to the last session: the concomitant temozolomide (75 mg/m^2 on 42 calendar days from the CRT start date) and the adjuvant cycles that start before the last session date (150 mg/m^2 in cycle 1, 200 mg/m^2 afterwards, 5 days on in 28-day cycles as scripts/patient_sensitivity_analysis.py defines them since 2026-09-17; the doses are those of fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json). chemo_decay_rate is fixed at 9.24 /day (below) and chemo_kill_rate spans 1e-5 to 1e-2 (the sweep space's 5e-5-1e-2 with the floor lowered, see _revision): with sub-01's schedule the total log kill runs from a null effect (MGMT-unmethylated tumours gain little from temozolomide, Hegi et al. 2005, NEJM 352:997) through the survival rule read off the 2026-09-14 sweep (a model core survives the treatment while the cumulative log kill stays below about 0.7 e-folds) to a kill comparable with the radiotherapy's maximum in-field log kill. The parametrisation (a kill rate per unit exposure, 1/day per mg/m^2) has no literature source of its own, and none is claimed for the floor; the range is set by the bounds on L.
_chemo_decay_rate: chemo_decay_rate is a fixed value, 9.24 /day: temozolomide's plasma half-life is about 1.8 h (Baker et al. 1999, Clin Cancer Res 5:309), ln 2 / 1.8 h = 9.24 /day. It is not fitted because it is confounded with chemo_kill_rate: the drug clears between the daily doses (e^-9.24 per day), so the exposure of every dose is dose / chemo_decay_rate and only the ratio chemo_kill_rate / chemo_decay_rate reaches the response.
_radiotherapy: rt_alpha (1e-5-0.1 /Gy, log-uniform) is the linear coefficient of the linear-quadratic log kill E(x) = rt_alpha d(x) + rt_beta d(x)^2 per fraction, d(x) = rt_dose / 30 the per-fraction dose of the patient's warped dose map; rt_beta = rt_alpha / rt_alpha_beta_ratio is derived by the solver and is not a config entry. rt_alpha_beta_ratio is fixed at 8 Gy, the midpoint of the sweep space's 4-12 Gy (clinical GBM estimates: Pedicini et al. 2014, Strahlenther Onkol 190:925: alpha/beta = 8 Gy, 95 % CI 5.0-10.8 Gy), which the sensitivity analysis found inert. The cap 0.1 /Gy is the sweep space's (in-vivo effective values are about 0.01 /Gy, Rockne et al. 2010, Phys Med Biol 55:3271); the floor 1e-5 /Gy is a further decade and a half below the sweep space's 5e-4 so that a radiotherapy without a measurable effect on the model core is inside the range, see _revision. No literature value is claimed for the floor.
_fixed: Fixed values and why: seed_peak_density 0.6, rt_alpha_beta_ratio 8 Gy and diffusivity_ratio 10 (the white-to-gray-matter diffusivity ratio, the geometric centre of the sweep space's 1-100) because the sensitivity analysis found the three inert on the agreement QoIs (see _revision); chemo_decay_rate 9.24 /day because it is confounded with chemo_kill_rate (see _chemo_decay_rate); gaussian_seed_scale 1 so that seed_sigma_mm is in mm (see _seed_band). Every value is written into every run config (seed_peak_density excepted, which the script consumes) and overrides the base config's.
_units: front_speed_mm_per_day mm/day; front_width_mm mm; the derived white_matter_diffusivity mm^2/day and rho 1/day; seed_sigma_mm mm (the standard deviation of the seed profile); the derived gaussian_seed_diffusion_time mm^2 and gaussian_seed_mass density times mm^3; growth_length_mm mm; the derived preop_time days from the seed to the pre-op scan; seed_bbox_x/y/z dimensionless coordinates on the seedable voxels' bounding box; rt_alpha 1/Gy; chemo_kill_rate 1/day per mg/m^2; seed_peak_density a cell density (fraction of the carrying capacity); diffusivity_ratio dimensionless; rt_alpha_beta_ratio Gy; chemo_decay_rate 1/day.
_sources: Every range and scale not changed in _revision is that of sailor_patient_v2_search_space.json (2026-09-17), which follows stupp_fkpp_sigma_v2_search_space.json (growth speed, seed, diffusivity_ratio, chemo_decay_rate, rt_alpha_beta_ratio, gaussian_seed_scale): front_speed_mm_per_day 0.03-0.25 mm/day and front_width_mm 1-8 mm, see _growth_band (the cohort estimates of scripts/parameter_range.txt, rho 0.0089-0.34 /day and D 0.0071-2.1 mm^2/day, give lambda = sqrt(D / rho) from 0.14 to 15 mm with a typical 3 mm; radial expansion rates reported for untreated glioblastoma reach about 0.2 mm/day); seed_sigma_mm 5-16 mm, a design choice, see _seed_band; the rt_alpha and chemo_kill_rate caps, see _radiotherapy and _chemo. The floors of the pre-op interval (7 days), rt_alpha (1e-5 /Gy) and chemo_kill_rate (1e-5 /day per mg/m^2) and the fixed values of seed_peak_density, rt_alpha_beta_ratio and diffusivity_ratio are the 2026-09-25 choices of _revision; no literature value is claimed for them.
